simple.meaning: לֶקַח (leqach) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, something received , i.e. (mentally) instruction (whether on the part of the teacher or hearer); also (in an active and sinister sense) inveiglement.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: לֶקַח (H3948) appears 9 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:2, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Job, Proverbs, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לֶקַח (H3948) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לֶקַח (H3948) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לֶקַח (leqach) / H3948 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:2, Job 11:4, Proverbs 1:5, Proverbs 4:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, something received , i.e. (mentally) instruction (whether on the part of the teacher or hearer); also (in an active and sinister sense) inveiglement
definitions.full: H3948. leqach לֶ֫קַח noun masculine Prov 4:2 learning, teaching ( concrete; probably what is received ); — ׳ל absolute Isa 29:24 5 t.; suffix לִקְחִי Deut 32:3 ; Job 11:4 ; לִקְחָהּ Prov 7:21 ; — 1 instruction , subjective, as personal acquirement; לֶ֑קַח יִלְמְדוּ Isa 29:24 , they shall learn instruction (|| בִּינָה ); לֶ֑קַח וְיוֺסֶף Prov 1:5 a wise man will hear and will increase (his) learning , so 9:9 . 2 teaching , object, as thing taught, לִקְחִי כַּמָּטָר יַעֲרֹף Deut 32:2 (|| אִמְרָתִי ), Job 11:4 ; ׳ל לָכֶם נָתַתִּי טוֺב Prov 4:2 ; also = teaching-power, persuasiveness , ל יוֺסִיף שְׂפָתַיִם ׳מֶתֶק 16:21 sweetness of lips increaseth persuasiveness (see מתק ), לֶקַח יוֺסִיף שְׂפָתָיו וְעַל 16:23 ; in bad sense, of seductive words of adulteress, ל ׳בְּרֹב 7:21 (|| שְׂפָתֶיהָ בְּחֵלֶק ).

occurrences.englishText: My doctrine will drop as the rain.
For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure.
that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning;
for I give you sound learning.
With persuasive words, she led him astray.
Instruct a wise person, and he will be still wiser.
The wise in heart shall be called prudent.
The heart of the wise instructs his mouth,
They also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will receive instruction.”
